hero.tagline: No. Carter's death is scripted — it happens on every single playthrough.
hero.intro: Here's exactly what happens, why the game makes you feel like it was your fault, and which characters you can actually save.

straightAnswer.heading: The Straight Answer
straightAnswer.callout: **Carter dies.** There is no QTE, dialogue option, or hidden path that prevents it. He dies in a scripted event at the end of Episode 1 and it is going to happen **every single time** you play. Do not waste time reloading checkpoints trying to save him.

whyGuilt.heading: Why the Game Makes You Think You Could Have Saved Him
whyGuilt.paragraph: This is deliberate. The game frames Carter's death like a consequence of a choice you made, and plenty of players spend an hour reloading checkpoints before they accept the truth. That feeling of “maybe I could have saved him” is exactly what Supermassive wanted — it's how the game establishes stakes for the five characters who *can* die by your choices.

whatHappens.heading: What Actually Happens to Carter and Simms
whatHappens.summary: ⚠ Spoilers — click to expand the death scene details
paragraphs: Both deaths are hard-coded into the Episode 1 narrative. **Carter** dies in a scripted event at the end of the chapter, no matter what you do earlier. **Simms** is corrupted by the alien Growth and her death is equally unavoidable.
Simms's story doesn't end there, though — she appears in later episodes as a **mimic**, not the real Simms. That reveal only works because she actually died in Episode 1.

This is intentional design. The Dark Pictures Anthology games feature 5 playable characters in co-op mode, and Directive 8020 has 6 crew members total. Carter and Simms exist as narrative catalysts — their deaths establish the stakes and motivate the surviving five. The math doesn't work any other way.

canSave.heading: The 5 Characters You Can Save
canSave.intro: Focus your energy on the five playable characters — all of them can reach the end alive:
canSave.footnote: Keeping all five alive — plus identifying the duplicate Eisele in Episode 6 and exposing the clone program in Episode 8 — unlocks the true ending, “Eisele the Humanitarian.”

faqs.a: No. Carter dies in a scripted event at the end of Episode 1 on every playthrough. There is no QTE, dialogue option, or hidden path that prevents it.

faqs.q: Can you save Carter and Simms?
faqs.a: No. Both have scripted deaths in Episode 1. Simms is corrupted by the alien Growth, and she later appears as a mimic — not the real Simms.

faqs.q: Which characters can survive in Directive 8020?
faqs.a: The 5 playable characters: Young, Stafford, Eisele, Cernan, and Cooper. All five can reach the end alive and unlock the true ending.

sections.heading: What was corrected
sections.text: The earlier scene-specific instructions and first-person playthrough claims are withdrawn pending verification. No replacement guess is being presented as a proven solution.

sections.heading: How to proceed
sections.text: Use the current in-game prompts and Turning Points options. Official material confirms revisiting key decisions, but does not document every scene or guarantee a particular ending. This page will need a verified scene-by-scene account before its route advice is restored.
